comment: Parameters of the aggregated dataset for our own detector model (issue #46/#50). build_dataset.py only executes this file. 'expected' pins what a run has to produce; after a deliberate change copy the new values from the error message and raise 'version'.
sources_comment: All of these need data/sources/<source>/rows.jsonl (fetch_sources.py, collect_human.py). The order decides which of two duplicates is kept: the earlier source wins.

drop.reason: 88% of the human answers are tokenised through and through ("do n't", "( word )", "URL_0") and cannot be put back together reliably. The ChatGPT answers are clean, but without their human side they would be 16,000 forum texts of one class; the sub-source is left out as a whole (decision of 2026-10-11). Human ELI5 answers without the artefact come from MAGE.

max_ai_per_group_comment: RAID has 34 generations per human document. Per document this many are kept, chosen by a seeded hash and from different generators. The held-out generators are kept whole: they only exist in the test part, where every row counts.
tokenised_comment: A text with at least this many signs of tokeniser spacing, absolute and per 100 words, is dropped whatever its source or class. Fewer signs are repaired by normalise().

duplicates.comment: Similarity = common 5-word sequences / those of the shorter text, over all sequences. From 'duplicate' on one text stays and the groups are merged; from 'related' on the two texts must be on the same side of the split.

split.comment: Shares of the hash range per source group, not of the number of groups: a group keeps its side when data is added.
